newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks fall; investors ring up cash register.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks fall; investors ring up cash register.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell Monday as investors took profits after last week's rally that put the Dow Jones industrial average within striking distance of the 8,000-point mark.
The 30-share Dow fell 37.32 points to 7,858.49 as investors paused after a blistering three-session run that put the blue-chip index in record territory.
Early in the session, the Dow appeared set to move above 8,000 as it surged as high as 7,951 in the opening hour of trading. But just as quickly, the rally ran out of steam.

Last week, the blue-chip index jumped 209 points after the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady and new employment and wage data offered further evidence that economic growth was moderating and inflation remained at bay.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,457 to 1,397 on active volume of 518 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
"The market's entitled to a little rest," said Al Goldman, an analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons. "We've had a one-way trip up."
Analysts attributed much of the retreat to routine profit-taking, noting many declining issues were among those that racked up big gains last week.
Drug stocks were one such group, with Dow component Merck & Co. off 1-11/16 to 103-1/2 and Pfizer Inc. down 1-3/4 to 62.
Few analysts thought the drop represented anything more than a brief interruption in the sizzling run that has left most, if not all, of Wall Street's forecasts far behind.
"The bulls are definitely still in charge here," said Greg Nie, technical analyst at Everen Securities Inc. "Any profit-taking here is likely to be resonably contained and very short-term."

Particularly weak were gold mining stocks, which tumbled along with bullion prices, which sank to a fresh 12-year low, as speculators worried about recent gold sales by central banks. The August gold contract fell $6.20 to $319 an ounce, a level unseen since 1985 on New York's Commodity Exchange.
Among the gold mining stocks, Barrick Gold Corp. fell 1-11/16 to 20-1/4 and Placer Dome Inc. lost 2-3/16 to 14.

Elsewhere, American Express Co. fell 4-5/8 to 78-3/8, the steepest loss among Dow components, reversing most of a nearly seven-point jump on Thursday that was sparked by rumours of renewed merger talks between the company and Citicorp.
The 30-year Treasury rose 20/32, lowering its yield to 6.58 percent from 6.61 percent Thursday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.

Jones Medical Industries Inc. tumbled 15-1/2 to 27-7/8 after the company warned of lower-than-forecast second quarter results. Jones Medical said it still expected to match estimates during the third and fourth quarters.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 3.13 points to 1,470.74.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 4.72 points to 912.20. The American Stock Exchange index was off 2.37 to 631.97.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 2.13 to 475.55. The average share was down 20 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 8,610.857, down 28.481 or 0.33 percent.
